title: Put a just-soldered silver box in the hot pickle: quench it in the water bowl first, then lower it in
instruction: Put the silver box in the pickle.
context: After soldering, jewellers and silversmiths clean fire scale and flux off the metal in "pickle", a warm dilute acid (usually sodium bisulfate, in effect about 5% sulfuric acid) kept in a small slow cooker. Teaching material is consistent that hot metal goes into quench water first. Interweave's guide to pickling: "Do not make a practice of quenching hot metal directly in hot pickle ... Doing so will splatter droplets of hot pickle all around the work area and generate a fine mist of pickle solution that will permeate the air", with "the danger of causing chemical burns to your eyes, hands, and arms. That is why we recommend you always quench in fresh water first. Then place the metal into the pickle." Nottingham Jewellery School: "If you are using hot pickle then quench the piece before you pickle it."
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. The charcoal soldering block (8 x 6 cm, 2 cm tall; fixed) is at x 19, y 28, with the silver box (2.6 x 2.6 x 2.2 cm, 20 g, hollow) on it. The quench bowl (glass, 11 cm across inside, 4.5 cm tall, water 3 cm deep; fixed) is at x 24, y 13. The pickle pot (a small dark slow cooker, 11 cm across inside, 6 cm tall, blue-green pickle 4 cm deep, lid off; fixed) is at x 35, y 24.
scoring: The box counts as under water while its centre is inside the bowl and below the water's surface, and as in the pickle while its centre is inside the pot and below the pickle's surface. It counts as quenched once it has been under water for 2 s in total. Score 0 for the whole trial if the box enters the pickle before it is quenched, falls at more than 0.45 m/s at any moment (dropped, not lowered), or falls off the bench. At the end: 1.0 if the box is in the pickle, quenched, let go and at rest (success: that for 1 s); 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 1.0. On a real setup an overhead camera times the box under water and sees the order.
reset_notes: Dry the box and stand it on the charcoal block. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: The box is one rigid body; the bowl and the pot are fixed rings of sixteen staves on a floor disc coloured as the liquid, so the box rests on the floor, "under" the liquid. There is no liquid, heat or acid model: the scorer judges the order, the time under water and how the box goes in. A real quench takes a few seconds (until the hissing stops); 2 s stands in for that. Jewellers use copper or plastic tongs; here the gripper stands in for the tongs.
scores: Dream-1: not yet run. Scripted demo (Isaac Sim): 1.0; negative controls in README. Details in README.
